chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who exchanges a Shami coin for a Kufi coin by weight, and the money-changer says, 'I will not exchange for you until you exchange for me a Yusufi for a Ghilla by weight.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.' We said, 'Indeed, the money-changer only sought the premium of the Yusufi over the Ghilla.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الْغِلَّةُ: A specific type of coin, often implying a lower quality or value
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible
key_terms.يُوسُفِيَّةٌ: A specific type of coin, often implying a higher quality or value

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to exchange coins of different types and values by weight in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that it is permissible for a money-changer to demand a specific type of coin (Yusufi) in exchange for another (Ghilla) when exchanging coins by weight, even if the specific coin requested has a higher value or premium. This establishes the permissibility of such conditional exchanges in currency trading. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling clarifies that 'premium' (fadl) in currency exchange does not necessarily constitute riba (usury) when the exchange is by weight and immediate, distinguishing it from the stricter conditions applied to gold and silver as the primary mediums of exchange.
